subject: Re: Help for syntax: Control for clustered data = MIMIC model?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Help for syntax: Control for clustered data = MIMIC model?
parts:
I am using dummy variables. I am unsure if my syntax is correct in this regard:

I would regress all the observed (not latent) variables in your model on the dummies, so there is not a restrictive assumption of measurement invariance across schools.  Also, the default should be conditional.x=TRUE, meaning that the estimator's criterion will be to reproduce the residual polychoric correlation matrix after partialling out the exogenous dummies.  Your hypothesized model is better able to do that if it in fact partials out all the school dummies from the observed variables. 

FYI, you could automatically add them to the syntax this way:

model1 <- '
  KF.lv =~ KF1 + KF2 + KF3 + KF4 + KF5 + KF6 + KF7 + KF8 + KF9 + KF10
  KU.lv =~ KU1 + KU2 + KU3 + KU4 + KU5 + KU6 + KU7 + KU8
  KA.lv =~ KA1 + KA2 + KA3 + KA4 + KA5 + KA6 + KA7 + KA8 + KA9 + KA10
'
obsNames <- lavNames(lavaanify(model1))
dumNames <- paste0("School_", 1:22)
(exoPaths <- outer(X = obsNames, Y = dumNames,
                   FUN = paste, sep = " ~ "))
dwls_cfa <-cfa(c(model1, exoPaths), ...)
 
I have read in other posts that this warning message may not necessarily be a problem.

It is probably fine, unless there are other signs of lack of identification.


If checking for school is not possible because of the identification of the model, I would check for the school type (three school types and thus only 2 dummy variables).

Certainly fewer parameters, but that would not account for clustering effects, so you could not trust your SEs or tests.  The conditional.x=TRUE approach does help (e.g., in small samples) to reduce burden on the estimator, because the "observed" covariance matrix only includes the endogenous variables.


Then one last question: is the model I specified already a MIMIC model?

Technically, if you have observed variables as both predictors and outcomes of common factors, then it is a MIMIC. But not really in the sense of interpretation, because the school dummies are not causal "indicators", just control variables.  

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

Warning:
In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix

From researching the warning, I could not deduce whether or not it is irrelevant to my case. If the warning is relevant, then I don't know what I would have to change. Well, maybe something with exo. Dummies?

Estimating all those effects increases the number of estimated parameters, but your model was already large to begin with.  You now have fewer than 2 subjects per parameter you want to estimate.  

  Number of model parameters                                           731

                                                      

                                                                               Used       Total

  Number of observations                                 1330        1420


The weight matrix used to calculate SEs can be un-invertible in (relatively) small samples, in which case the Moore-Penrose generalized inverse in MASS::ginv() is used (without being able to guarantee its quality).
